verified_key_information_units.information: Investments totalled EUR 3.5 million in H1 2026 (versus EUR 12.0 million in H1 2025), mainly for ferry engine replacement, upgrades to the quay at Paldiski South Harbour, and IT infrastructure. Q2 investments were EUR 2.3 million (versus EUR 8.4 million in Q2 2025).

As of 30 June 2026, total assets were EUR 615.0 million (down from EUR 622.1 million), loans and borrowings were EUR 173.4 million (stable), total liabilities were EUR 247.4 million (up from EUR 241.2 million), equity was EUR 367.7 million (down from EUR 380.9 million), and cash and cash equivalents were EUR 27.6 million (down from EUR 32.0 million).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Interim Condensed Consolidated Statement of Financial Position page 18

verified_key_information_units.information: Significant Q2 2026 events: (a) Tallinn City Council adopted detailed plans for Terminal A and D areas; (b) Icebreaker Botnica completed a 20-day North Sea project; (c) A EUR 32 million unsecured loan agreement was signed with OP Corporate Bank; (d) Up to 485 additional Regula ferry trips were ordered for summer 2026; (e) A EUR 19.2 million dividend was paid (85% of 2025 profit).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Significant Events section pages 15-17; Dividends section page 14

candidate_sentences.text: Revenue growth was mainly supported by a EUR 0.9 million increase in charter-fee revenue, as icebreaker Botnica recorded 130 charter days versus 110 in the comparative period, including a 20-day North Sea project in June.
Ferry-service revenue increased EUR 0.3 million due to tariff indexation and compensation for additional Regula trips.
The Group paid EUR 19.2 million in dividends, resulting in a EUR 4.4 million reduction in cash to EUR 27.6 million and operating cash flow of EUR 18.2 million, down from EUR 26.3 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: At 30 June 2026, market capitalisation was EUR 335.06 million (versus EUR 340.85 million at 31 December 2025). The share price closed at EUR 1.274 (versus EUR 1.296 at the start of 2026), with 22,559 shareholders (67.0% held by the Republic of Estonia).

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K3, and K4 are fully covered with supporting details in the candidate. K7 is partially present, covering the Botnica project, Regula trips, and dividend payment, but missing the Tallinn City Council plan adoption and the OP Corporate Bank loan agreement. K5 (investment details), K6 (balance sheet items), and K8 (market capitalisation and share price data) are entirely missing. The summary captures most high-importance financial performance drivers and profitability changes, but lacks several medium/high importance items, resulting in a 'Generally yes' assessment.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. All statements logically follow one another without contradictions. Revenue growth drivers (charter fees, electricity sales, ferry services) are clearly explained and contrasted with expense increases (fuel, electricity, maintenance). The profitability decline is consistently attributed to rising costs outweighing revenue gains. Organizational structure progresses logically from revenue to profitability metrics, then to expense breakdowns and finally to cash flow impacts. No material repetitions or logical gaps exist. The summary forms a clear narrative arc from top-line performance to bottom-line results with appropriate causal linkages throughout.
